olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Let $P(n)$ be the product of all nonzero digits of positive integer $n$. Compute $P(1)+P(2)+\cdots+P(2009)$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Circles $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$ intersect at $A,B$. Circle $\Gamma$ inside both, tangent to $\Gamma_1$ at $D$ and $\Gamma_2$ at $E$. $C$ = intersection of line $AB$ with $\Gamma$; $F=EC\cap\Gamma_2$; $G=DC\cap\Gamma_1$; $H,I$ = intersections of $DE$ with $\Gamma_1,\Gamma_2$. Prove $F,G,H,I$ are concyclic.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: 2009 boxes numbered $1,\ldots,2009$; some have stones. Players alternate (A first): choose nonempty box $i$, take $\geq 1$ stones and put them in box $i+1$ (if $i=2009$, stones are eliminated). Last to remove wins. (a) Start: 2009 stones in box 2. (b) Start: 1 stone in each box. Find winning strategies.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Place $1,\ldots,2009$ around a circle so absolute differences of neighbors are all distinct. (a) Is this possible with $1,\ldots,2009$? (b) Is it possible if one number is removed?
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2009

olympiad_full_name: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad
statement: Acute scalene $\triangle ABC$ with orthocenter $H$, circumcenter $O$; $E,F$ = feet of altitudes from $B,C$. $AO$ meets circumcircle at $G$; meets $FE,BC$ at $X,Y$. $Z$ = intersection of $AH$ with tangent to circumcircle at $G$. Prove $HX\parallel YZ$.
source: Central American and Caribbean Mathematical Olympiad 2009
